Class TomlBindings

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.toml.TomlBindings
public final class TomlBindings extends Object
The conversions that the code the annotation processor generates binds and writes values with. They are public for that code only: applications bind tables with Toml.bind(TomlTable, Class), and write records with Toml.toTable(Record).

Each conversion to a Java value takes a value and its TomlBindings.Context, which locates the value in the document, and throws a TomlMappingException at its path if the value does not convert.

Since:
0.1.0

    • table

      public static TomlTable table(TomlValue value, TomlBindings.Context context, String... keys)
      Returns a value that is a table, after checking that it has no other key than keys, unless the context ignores unknown keys.
      Parameters:
      value - the value
      context - the context of the value
      keys - the keys the table may have
      Returns:
      the table
      Throws:
      TomlMappingException - if value is not a table, or has another key that the context rejects
      NullPointerException - if an argument or a key is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if keys has the same key twice

    • asDuration

      public static Duration asDuration(TomlValue value, TomlBindings.Context context)
      Converts a string to a duration. The string is either:
      • in ISO-8601, as Duration.parse(CharSequence) reads it, such as "PT1M30S" or "-P2DT3H"; or
      • one or more amounts, each followed by its unit, the units in decreasing order and at most once each, after an optional - sign, such as "1h30m", "2.5s" or "-500ms". An amount is digits, optionally followed by a dot and more digits. The units are d (24 hours), h, m, s, ms, us and ns. The total must be a whole number of nanoseconds.
      Parameters:
      value - the value
      context - the context of the value
      Returns:
      the duration
      Throws:
      TomlMappingException - if value is not a string, or not a duration
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null
